newsitem.title: FRANCE: France detains Basque guerrilla leader.
newsitem.headline: France detains Basque guerrilla leader.

text.p: French police said on Wednesday they had detained the suspected former financier of the guerrilla group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).

Carlos Ibarguren Aguire, his wife and three other suspects were detained in three separate swoops in Saint-Jean-de-Luz and Bayonne in the French Basque region on warrants issued by anti-terrorist judge Laurence Le Vert.
One of the ETA's so-called historical leaders, Ibarguren Aguire, nicknamed "Nervios" (Highly-strung), is wanted in Spain on suspicion of extorting "revolutionary taxes" from businesses.
Believed to be in charge of the group's finances, he came to France last year after 12 years in exile in Brazil and was granted political refugee status by French authorities.
His arrest coincides with the trial in Paris of three top leaders of ETA, including the group's former operational chief Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia.
ETA, whose leaders often hide over the border in France, has killed some 800 people in Spain in a three-decade-long campaign for a separate Basque state.
